<thought>By retrieving the isotopic distributions of common organic elements, I can compare them to the observed pattern. The spectrum shows a dominant M peak at 276 Da with a series of smaller peaks up to M+8, indicating the presence of elements that have multiple stable isotopes (e.g., Cl, Br, S, Si). The relative intensities and spacing match the known patterns for chlorine (35Cl/37Cl, ~3:1 ratio) and bromine (79Br/81Br, ~1:1 ratio). No other element in the typical organic set (C, H, N, O, P) produces such a distinct multi‑peak pattern. Therefore, the elements that can be definitively identified from the isotope pattern are chlorine and bromine.> 
<final_answer>['Cl', 'Br']</final_answer>
